purpose: The per-module graph coverage verdict and the evidence behind each one. One test, stated once and applied to every module; where it cannot be satisfied the module is named with no verdict rather than passed on weaker evidence.
the_test: a class in the module's PRIMARY artifact, absent from every other module's artifacts
what_delivery_versus_coverage_mean: Delivery - that every staged JAR was handed to the frontend - is established by the total and injective staging manifest in cpg-input-inventory.json, not by this file. Coverage asks a different question: did THIS module's own code reach the graph, provably attributable to it. A shared package prefix cannot answer it, because every Spark module shares org.apache.spark and a prefix test lets one module vouch for a dozen absent ones.

presence_test_used.test: the witness must appear as an INTERNAL type declaration (cpg.typeDecl.isExternal(false))
presence_test_used.why_not_mere_presence: cpg.typeDecl carries a stub declaration for every type the processed bytecode references. This graph holds 52267 internal and 48610 external typeDecl fullNames, so a presence test over fullNames alone would accept a name no staged artifact ships. The measured instance is org.apache.spark.SparkFunSuite: present as a fullName, absent as bytecode, because the retained pre-shade streaming tests sibling references it while core's tests artifact - the only artifact that ships it - was excluded.

expected_absent_classes.name: org.apache.spark.SparkFunSuite
expected_absent_classes.verdict: ABSENT as bytecode; present only as an EXTERNAL stub reference

tests_artifact_exclusion_check.interpretation: Of the six test-only classes probed, five are absent from the graph entirely and one - org.apache.spark.SparkFunSuite - is present only as an external stub reference, so no excluded test artifact's bytecode reached the graph. Separately, the ONE retained pre-shade sibling of a tests artifact (original-spark-streaming_2.13-4.1.0-SNAPSHOT-tests.jar) did put streaming's test bytecode in the graph, and that is measured here rather than assumed: five of its classes are internal declarations with real method counts. cpg-input-inventory.json staging.exclusion.retained_test_bytecode records it.

<root>.verdict: NOT APPLICABLE - pom-packaging project, no primary artifact by design

evidence.why: this is a pom-packaging project: it has no primary artifact by design, so the primary-artifact coverage test does not apply to it. The only artifact it emitted is a -tests JAR from the test-jar goal (spark-parent_2.13-4.1.0-SNAPSHOT-tests.jar, 20,371 B), and that artifact is test-classified, so the staging exclusion removes it: this project contributes NOTHING to the graph input, which of_those_in_the_graph_input records as an empty list. It is the one producing module of the 39 with no staged artifact.
